rows.title: CT lawmakers still undecided whether to bolster home heating aid

rows.title: Report: CT ranks in bottom half of states in tax fairness
rows.standfirst: Though CT has eased tax burdens on the poor and middle class in recent years, it ranks behind 29 other states in one key fairness metric.

rows.title: Revenues tick upward as next CT budget debate nears
rows.standfirst: CT’s state government will have slightly more revenue next fiscal year, but that doesn’t mean legislators will get to spend it as they hoped.

rows.title: CT home heating aid remains on back burner despite cutbacks
rows.standfirst: The CT program that delivers winter assistance faces cutbacks, and lawmakers won’t decide whether to supplement funding before February.

rows.title: Progressive policy group urges CT to expand tax relief for families
rows.standfirst: CT Voices For Children urged CT legislators to establish a new tax credit for households with children that would help more than 80,000 kids.

rows.title: CT will bolster home heating aid funding in February, leaders say
rows.standfirst: CT Democratic leaders expect to introduce legislation next month to supplement winter heating assistance depleted by shrinking federal funds.

rows.title: CT social service groups seek $180M to offset some inflation loss
rows.standfirst: The CT Community Nonprofit Alliance is asking Gov. Ned Lamont for a funding boost — despite warnings of a tight state budget.

rows.title: A question of volatility: Are Connecticut’s fiscal guardrails in the right place?
rows.standfirst: The first in a three-part series about Connecticut’s fiscal guardrails and their impact not only on state reserves and debt, but also core programs like education and health care.

rows.title: Many core services are eroding as money goes to pensions
rows.standfirst: As the CT government piled up cash, many core services have slipped or remain in the dire straits they faced before the boom times.

rows.title: Constrained by guardrails, legislative session looms
rows.standfirst: The showdown foreseen by leaders of the Democratic majority could begin Feb. 7, when Gov. Ned Lamont proposes adjustments to the budget.

rows.title: Lamont’s modest revisions to CT budget quickly draw protests
